deposit_profile: A deposit address is one customer's: everything it sends goes to the wallets of one exchange (a sweep into a hot wallet), few outside addresses ever pay it, it never swaps on a DEX, and it is no token, pool, router or smart account.
hint: Answer: write every address in full (0x plus 40 characters), also when it repeats one named earlier and also when the user asks for shorter ones (name them instead); a transfer moves tokens, so write "tokens worth about N USD", never "sent N USD" or a $ figure; never draw the flows in text, ASCII or Mermaid, the host draws them. 0xfca4deb4a4a0f9182a2ae91502451005a818f66f carries no deposit mark: no SWEPT link and no cex_role. Say that the graph shows no sweep of it into a listed exchange hot wallet. That is not proof the address belongs to no exchange; its labels and its links say what else it is. Its behaviour, as the graph counts it: 8 addresses paid it (0 of them exchange wallets), it paid 4 addresses (0 of them exchange wallets), it swapped on 0 DEX pools, it approved 1 spender. What a deposit address does not do, and this one did: it paid 4 addresses that are no exchange wallet. Give these facts as the reason and no other: set no threshold of your own for payers, volume or sweeps. Asked how a deposit address behaves, what makes an address one or what rules one out, answer with deposit_profile.
